thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT: streaming-gateway (eu-west1) - sudden p95/p99 latency spike + SSE chunk stalls detected. Paging on-call.

eric.hansen: Got it, joining. What are the current p95/p99 numbers? :eyes:

incident-bot: p95 = 1.8s (baseline 200ms), p99 = 6.2s (baseline 600ms). Error rate is low but streaming tail latency and 'chunk-silence' alerts from edge-proxy are high. First anomalies at 1719999920.

sre_jenn: I'm seeing a lot of 499/timeout-ish logs from the proxy to collector: `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)` across several workers. Also client-backpressure events spiking in the gateway metrics.

oliver.k: Can you paste the short log sample? I want to see if it's socket-level or application-level buffering.

sre_jenn: Sure — truncated:
```
[2026-03-17T12:12:05Z] proxy/edge nginx: upstream timed out while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.45, server: streaming-gateway, request: "GET /sse/stream/abc HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.4.9.8:8080/stream", host: gateway.eu-west1.redwood.ai
```

maya.cs: We have two customers on EU region reporting choppy responses in-app. One mentions long pauses (10-20s) then catch-up. They flagged it as impacting interactive workflows.

eric.hansen: Looks like the proxy connections to the streaming backend are being stalled. Any recent deploys or config changes to the pool/keepalive? infra-amo, fyi.

infra-amo: No user-facing deploys in the last 2 hours. We did rotate a few edge instances 30m ago but health checks looked fine. I pulled kernel dmesg — no OOMs. Network EKS node metrics show increased socket backlog on a subset of nodes.

oliver.k: Could be slow consumers + connection windowing: when the client can't read fast enough, the backend's send buffers grow and upstream backs up, leading to proxy timeouts. Are we seeing high TCP retransmits or zero rwnd from client side?

sre_jenn: I checked TCPLISTEN stats — RX/TX queue depth on the backend pods shows write stalls. Also the streaming runtime reports many requests with long KV cache write durations around 8-12s during the spike.

eric.hansen: Immediate mitigation options: 1) force short-term fallback to non-streaming (polling) for affected routes; 2) increase proxy timeouts and keepalive pools; 3) evict slow clients via the gateway. Thoughts?

raj.oncall: I'm taking the page. I'll coordinate mitigations. Prioritize reducing customer-visible stalls quickly. I'll try #2 then #3 if needed.

maya.cs: Customers asked if there's a workaround short term — we can toggle feature-flag to disable SSE where we detect client slow-read, but that requires app-level change. Would prefer infra fixes first.

raj.oncall: Rolling a config bump on edge-proxy: `proxy_read_timeout` from 15s -> 45s and increase upstream keepalive connections per worker. Pushing now to eu-west1 canary nodes.

incident-bot: Deploy msg: edge-proxy-config-rollout started (canary 5%).

sre_jenn: After the canary config, canary logs show fewer 504/proxy timeouts but still some stalled chunks. p95 dropped to 1.2s in canary subset.

oliver.k: We should also enable the 'aggressive draining' flag on streaming-gateway that proactively closes connections when client rcv buffer doesn't advance for >5s. It reduces tail but may cause more reconnects.

raj.oncall: I'm enabling aggressive-drain on canaries for test. If stable for 5m, roll to 50%.

eric.hansen: Also flip on prefix/KV-response-cache for common prompt prefixes — reduces backend token emission rate for long-lived streams. Can that be done quickly?

oliver.k: Cache change requires minor config and safe to enable on canary routes. Doing that in parallel.

incident-bot: edge-proxy-config-rollout at 50% -> canary health OK. aggressive-drain enabled on canaries. Customer impact reports reduced jitter from one customer.

maya.cs: Confirmed — one customer (ACME Labs) reports much smoother streaming after config change. They still see occasional ~3s stalls but much better than 15s.

sre_jenn: Metrics: p95 now 650ms, p99 2.8s on canary group. Overall EU region p95 down to 1.1s but p99 still elevated.

eric.hansen: Next steps: (A) finish gradual rollout if no regressions, (B) follow-up offline root cause: why backend is accumulating write stalls — possible socket-layer backpressure from client proxies, or a GC stall in runtime causing periodic pauses. Capture perf traces from streaming runtime nodes during next spike window.

raj.oncall: Rolling to 100% now. I'll hand off to oliver for deep-dive. If p99 remains >2s in 15m, escalate to paging rotation.

oliver.k: Taking handoff for RCA. I'll collect goroutine stacks + tcpdump from affected pods and check for long syscalls and GC logs. Tagging this as follow-up postmortem.

maya.cs: Customer comms: I'll send an update: we mitigated immediate stalls with gateway config changes, investigating root cause. ETA for deeper RCA next 24–48h. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated): streaming-gateway p95/p99 returned near baseline after rollout. Monitoring for 1h. Severity: S2. Handing to oncall follow-up.

eric.hansen: Thanks team. Action items for postmortem: 1) capture and analyze tcp-level backpressure patterns, 2) evaluate default proxy timeouts vs keepalive pool sizing, 3) consider adaptive aggressive-drain heuristics tied to client read-rate metrics, 4) customer-facing postmortem draft.

oliver.k: Noted, will OWN RCA. Raj, please update runbook to include a quick checklist for similar future incidents (config roll + aggressive-drain + cache toggle).

raj.oncall: Will update runbook. Marking handoff complete — next oncall: raj.oncall -> oliver.k. :pager:

maya.cs: I'll follow up with affected customers with a short timeline and link to postmortem when ready.

incident-bot: Page cleared. Thread closed but follow-up tasks assigned.
